sources.citation: Krifka, Manfred. 2025. Demonstrative and anaphoric reference in Daakie (Ambrym, Vanuatu) with special focus on associative anaphors. Ms., lingbuzz/009009 (to appear in Te Reo), 29 pp.

sources.note: Fn. 2 orthography note only (accents denote higher vowels; labiovelars; prenasalized stops; long vowels doubled). Fn. 11 mentions 'emphatic stress and lengthening' of lasi 'big' for 'huge' (expressive emphasis, not a word-stress rule). Silent on word stress.

sources.citation: Krifka, Manfred (with Abel Taho, Paul Tomo et al.). 2017. Daa ne Daakie kevene. Ol Wod blong Daakie. Daakie Dictionary. Create Space (cc-by), 298 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Front matter pp.1-5 (Daakie/Bislama/English) and p.5 pronunciation chart (vowel and consonant tables only). Acute accents on headwords mark vowel quality (á=[æ], é=[e], ó=[o]), not stress; bracketed IPA forms carry no stress marks. Silent on stress.

sources.note: p.566-567: 'There is no grammatical description of Daakie.. a preliminary analysis of the modality system was presented by Krifka (2012)'. Nothing on stress.

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)

sources.citation: Krifka, Manfred. 2012. Notes on Daakie (Port Vato): Sounds and modality. Proceedings of AFLA 18 (Harvard, 2011), 46-65. Author's preprint, 21 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sect. 2 Phonology (2.1 consonants, 2.2 vowels and vowel fronting, 2.3 implications) read in full: inventories, length contrasts, allophonic fronting of back vowels after alveolars. No statement on stress or accent. Only trace: fn. 17 'realized as a two-syllable word, [kɔˈɔt]' (one stress-marked transcription, no rule).

sources.citation: Lynch, John & Terry Crowley. 2001. Languages of Vanuatu: A new survey and bibliography. Pacific Linguistics 517. Sect. 3.8.2(b) 'Port Vato', p.94.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online; also in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6211.V36 L96 2001)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6211.V36 L96 2001
sources.note: 'This communalect is also poorly known. Tryon (1976) includes a single wordlist.. Paton (1973) includes a substantial number of Port Vato equivalents.. Paton (1971a:105-118) includes a number of paradigms.' Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Paton, W. F. 1971. Ambrym (Lonwolwol) Grammar. Pacific Linguistics B-19. (Glottolog lists pp.105-118 'Pronouns' for Daakie.)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: The p.12 accent statement ('There is no apparent rule or uniformity of accent') describes Lonwolwol, not Port Vato; Port Vato (PV) appears only as a comparative column in paradigms (pp.105-118). No Daakie stress statement.

sources.citation: Krifka, Manfred. n.d. (2012-). Preliminary grammar sketch of Daakie. Unpublished, DoBeS/TLA West Ambrym deposit (Krifka, von Prince & Hosni project, VolkswagenStiftung).

sources.note: The only known grammar sketch of the language; a DoBeS sketch would normally open with phonology including a stress statement. Existence attested by the 2012 DoBeS poster ('still preliminary grammar sketches of Dalkalaen and Daakie').
